content.content: 1 --- 2 title: connection 3 description: API Reference for the connection function. 4 --- 5 6 The `connection()` function allows you to indicate rendering should wait for an incoming user request before continuing. 7 8 It's useful when a component doesn't use [Request-time APIs](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) like `cookies` or `headers`, but still needs to produce different output per request, such as `Math.random()` or `new Date()`. 9 10 ```ts filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 11 import { connection } from 'next/server' 12 13 export default async function Page() { 14 await connection() // prerendering stops here 15 // the following code only runs at request time 16 const rand = Math.random() 17 return {rand} 18 } 19 ``` 20 21 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 22 import { connection } from 'next/server' 23 24 export default async function Page() { 25 await connection() // prerendering stops here 26 // the following code only runs at request time 27 const rand = Math.random() 28 return {rand} 29 } 30 ``` 31 32 ## Examples 33 34 ### Synchronous database drivers 35 36 Queries from synchronous database drivers like `better-sqlite3` complete during prerendering. If you are not already using Request-time APIs, call `connection()` before your query to exclude them from prerendering: 37 38 ```ts filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher 39 import { connection } from 'next/server' 40 import Database from 'better-sqlite3' 41 42 const db = new Database('app.db') 43 44 export async function getVisitorCount() { 45 await connection() 46 return db.prepare('SELECT value FROM counters WHERE name = ?').get('visitors') 47 } 48 ``` 49 50 ```js filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher 51 import { connection } from 'next/server' 52 import Database from 'better-sqlite3' 53 54 const db = new Database('app.db') 55 56 export async function getVisitorCount() { 57 await connection() 58 return db.prepare('SELECT value FROM counters WHERE name = ?').get('visitors') 59 } 60 ``` 61 62 Now any component that calls `getVisitorCount()` will be excluded from prerendering, along with the rest of its output. 63 64 ## Reference 65 66 ### Type 67 68 ```jsx 69 function connection(): Promise 70 ``` 71 72 ### Parameters 73 74 - The function does not accept any parameters. 75 76 ### Returns 77 78 - The function returns a `void` Promise. It is not meant to be consumed. 79 80 ## Good to know 81 82 - `connection` replaces [`unstable_noStore`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unstable_noStore) to better align with the future of Next.js. 83 - The function is only necessary when dynamic rendering is required and common Request-time APIs are not used. 84 85 ### Version History 86 87 | Version | Changes | 88 | ------------ | ------------------------ | 89 | `v15.0.0` | `connection` stabilized. | 90 | `v15.0.0-RC` | `connection` introduced. | 91

It's useful when a component doesn't use [Request-time APIs](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) like `cookies` or `headers`, but still needs to produce different output per request, such as `Math.random()` or `new Date()`. ```ts filename="app/page.tsx" switcher import { connection } from 'next/server' export default async function Page() { await connection() // prerendering stops here // the following code only runs at request time const rand = Math.random() return {rand} } ``` ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher import { connection } from 'next/server' export default async function Page() { await connection() // prerendering stops here // the following code only runs at request time const rand = Math.random() return {rand} } ``` ## Examples ### Synchronous database drivers Queries from synchronous database drivers like `better-sqlite3` complete during prerendering. If you are not already using Request-time APIs, call `connection()` before your query to exclude them from prerendering: ```ts filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher import { connection } from 'next/server' import Database from 'better-sqlite3' const db = new Database('app.db') export async function getVisitorCount() { await connection() return db.prepare('SELECT value FROM counters WHERE name = ?').get('visitors') } ``` ```js filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher import { connection } from 'next/server' import Database from 'better-sqlite3' const db = new Database('app.db') export async function getVisitorCount() { await connection() return db.prepare('SELECT value FROM counters WHERE name = ?').get('visitors') } ``` Now any component that calls `getVisitorCount()` will be excluded from prerendering, along with the rest of its output. ## Reference ### Type ```jsx function connection(): Promise ``` ### Parameters - The function does not accept any parameters. ### Returns - The function returns a `void` Promise. It is not meant to be consumed. ## Good to know - `connection` replaces [`unstable_noStore`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unstable_noStore) to better align with the future of Next.js. - The function is only necessary when dynamic rendering is required and common Request-time APIs are not used. ### Version History | Version | Changes | | ------------ | ------------------------ | | `v15.0.0` | `connection` stabilized. | | `v15.0.0-RC` | `connection` introduced. |

12:Cache Components enables component and function-level caching using the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive. Data fetching is dynamic by default, and you choose what to cache at the page, component, or function level. Next.js prerenders a static HTML shell that is served immediately while dynamic content streams in when ready, letting you mix static and dynamic content within a single route.
25:export default nextConfig
36:Additionally, `cacheComponents` implements **[Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prerendering-ppr)** as the default behavior in the App Router.
